condition: Occult anastomotic leak in an older patient on a beta-blocker and steroids (day 4)
summary: 79-year-old woman, day 4 after right hemicolectomy, on bisoprolol and prednisolone: afebrile, new confusion, new AF at 104, distension and vomiting, CRP 245 and rising — leak until proven otherwise.

inputs.chiefComplaint: New confusion and irregular pulse after bowel operation
inputs.hpi: Day 4 after laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for caecal cancer. Confused overnight, pulled at her cannula. New irregular pulse this morning. Vomited twice, abdomen swelling, no flatus since yesterday. Takes bisoprolol for hypertension and prednisolone 7.5 mg for polymyalgia rheumatica.

exam.general: Drowsy, disorientated to time. Irregular pulse 104, BP 118/70, RR 22, SpO2 95% on air, T 37.3°C.
exam.abdomen: Distended, mild generalised tenderness, no rebound. Wounds clean. Quiet bowel sounds.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspected anastomotic leak (occult) — day 4 after right hemicolectomy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Day 4: new delirium, new AF, ileus and rising CRP 245 despite no fever (beta-blocker, steroids). Anastomotic leak until proven otherwise — CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast, sepsis screen, steroid cover.

mustNotMiss.note: Older patients on beta-blockers or steroids may not mount fever or tachycardia; new AF, delirium and rising CRP after bowel surgery are leak signs.

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Negation-aware matching (NegEx-style) in clinical-inference.ts exam()/hasRadResult() and triage rules.ts (see findings/hpb.md gap 1); gate operative-plan cascades on the working diagnosis.

guideline.name: ISREC definition and grading of anastomotic leakage after anterior resection
guideline.section: Grade A: no change in management; Grade B: active intervention without relaparotomy (antibiotics, radiological drainage); Grade C: relaparotomy
guideline.citation: Rahbari NN, Weitz J, Hohenberger W, et al. Surgery. 2010;147:339–51.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — management of intra-abdominal infections
guideline.section: Early source control; CT for diagnosis; percutaneous drainage for accessible collections; relaparotomy for diffuse peritonitis; empirical antibiotics by severity and local resistance
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Chichom-Mefire A, Labricciosa FM, et al. World J Emerg Surg. 2017;12:29.

guideline.name: NICE CG103 — Delirium: prevention, diagnosis and management in hospital and long-term care
guideline.section: Identify and manage underlying causes (infection, hypoxia, dehydration, pain, urinary retention, constipation, medication including opioids and anticholinergics); non-pharmacological measures first; short-term antipsychotic only if distressed or a risk to self/others; multicomponent prevention for people at risk (age ≥65, cognitive impairment)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Delirium (CG103). London: NICE; 2010 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: AAGBI/RCP/SfE guideline — glucocorticoids in the peri-operative period for adrenal insufficiency
guideline.section: Patients on ≥5 mg prednisolone (or equivalent) for >4 weeks are at risk of adrenal insufficiency: hydrocortisone at induction and continued cover until eating and drinking, then usual dose; do not omit usual glucocorticoid
guideline.citation: Woodcock T, Barker P, Daniel S, et al. Anaesthesia. 2020;75:654–63.

rationale: Permutation: atypical leak — afebrile, masked tachycardia, presenting as delirium, new AF and ileus. Tests that leak stays in the differential and CT is suggested.
